terms.description: The primarily affected object or matter of the notice represented as an item (e.g., a spatial plan title, a collective agreement name, or a specific piece of property).
A generic person field used when the primarily affected entity in the title can be either a natural individual or a legal corporation.
The primarily affected corporate body, company, or organization acting as the main legal entity in the publication title.
The primarily affected individual or human being acting as the main natural person in the publication title.
The designated legal representative, liquidator, or administrator of the primarily affected legal entity or debtor.
A secondarily affected corporate organization, such as a corporate creditor, claimant, or secondary party to a registry change.
A secondarily affected party (natural or legal), typically representing a creditor, a co-claimant, or an opposing party in a dispute.
The authorized legal representative or agent of the secondarily affected entity.
A rich-text or text-area field containing descriptive project information, conditional terms, or additional material text of a notice.
An attribute list defining the specific sub-category or variant of the business case (e.g., type of plan, type of project, or type of capital reduction).
An attribute list identifying the exact nature of a registry mutation, such as a change of corporate name or relocation of a registered office.
An attribute list defining the procedural framework of the case (e.g., summary vs. ordinary bankruptcy proceedings, or specific usage categories).
Refers to the political (federal) level to which the announcement relates.
A standardized closed attribute list classifying the category of the issuing body (e.g., judicial, executive, or municipal body).
A standardized closed attribute list classifying the category of the executive or administrative authority handling the file.
The free-text name of the specific department, office, or procurement unit in charge of executing the underlying proceedings.
The free-text name of the specific body, department, or court that officially issued the ruling, order, or decree.
The free-text name of the specific body, department, or court that officially requested a case.
The name of a petitioning party or applicant in cases where they are not classified as the primary legal entity of the notice.
The authorized legal representative, agent, or attorney representing the non-primary applicant.
The selling party, transferor, or alienator involved in a property transfer or asset conveyance transaction.
The receiving party, buyer, or beneficiary in a structural property transfer or procurement distribution.
The calendar date marking the official commencement, registration, or entry into force of a status, permit, or entry.
The final calendar date marking the expiration, deletion, or formal end of a status, permit, or legal moratorium.
The precise calendar date on which a legal entity, corporation, or partnership was formally dissolved.
The official calendar date on which a matter, ruling, or decree was formally decided, adopted, or ordered by an authority or voting body.
The calendar date on which a formal petition, parliamentary motion, or administrative request was officially filed.
The calendar date on which a specific document, registry daily-journal entry, or title was officially issued.
A plain-text time field or timestamp utilized for meeting hours, specific deadlines, or extended date remarks.
A structured postal address formatted in accordance with the official Swiss eCH-0010 standard.
Geostationary coordinates delivered as a URL or structured string to render points or perimeters on an external mapping system.
The official administrative tracking or serial number assigned to a specific daily-journal or registry entry.
A generic string field used for names, titles of objects, or new naming conventions that do not represent primary entities.
A text field or cross-reference key referencing an earlier related publication, prior notice, or previous entry in the system.
A text-area field describing the previous or existing statutory purpose of a corporation prior to its mutation or liquidation.
The official municipality or political location of a corporation's registered corporate seat.
A mandatory attached document (typically PDF) that contains the main body or official legal text of the publication itself.
Supplementary files, images, or maps uploaded to support and document the primary structured text of the notice.
A valid external hyperlink directing users to supplementary dossiers, official external platforms, or complete project files.
The calendar date on which a specific case has been withdrawn.
A text-area field with information to an event
This drop-down menu is used to specify the type of an environmental element,  such as the type of land use.
Using this drop-down menu, the publishing entity provides an assessment of whether the announcement is archival.
The date on which a decree or order comes into force
A number used to categorise or organise announcements within a particular announcement type, which can be used to sort them in the gazette.
Categories of Swiss Internal Law (1-9)
